issues.title: Requirement for "scim" scope in access token
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
https://github.com/jischr/scim-ipsie-profiles/blob/c289a468cd17d84b1878d9c33494e8c58e1559cb/draft-schreiber-ipsie-scim-al1-profile.md#L112

OAuth doesn't define scope names, which leads to a few thoughts:

1. Should this requirement be changed to say something to the effect of "must contain scopes that don't grant permission for actions outside of the SCIM service provider"? 

2. As part of SCIM-related work in IPSIE, should we try to define specific scopes or a framework for designing scopes that would scale beyond users and groups?

3. "scim" is still pretty broad, versus something like scim.groups.read or scim.users.readwrite - definitely feels more granular than a lot of implementations have today, but if we've got a chance to raise the bar, this sort of approach might be worth including.

comments.author: jischr
comments.body: https://github.com/openid/sharedsignals/issues/299

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body:
Decision: remove the bullet requiring the access token to include the "scim" scope and not grant broader permissions.

Access tokens may be opaque to the Identity Service, so the token's contents cannot be checked by the Identity Service or by a conformance test. OAuth also does not define scope names, so "scim" carries no standard meaning.

Separately, there may be a need for a standardized set of scopes for SCIM and other identity management APIs, or a broader framework for authorization into those kinds of systems. That would be its own piece of work rather than something this bullet can express.

The removal will be made in a PR that references this issue.

issues.title: IPSIE "roles" vs SCIM "groups" statement incorrect
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
https://github.com/jischr/scim-ipsie-profiles/blob/c289a468cd17d84b1878d9c33494e8c58e1559cb/draft-schreiber-ipsie-scim-al1-profile.md#L197-L198

SCIM has three distinct concepts currently - Groups, which are a resource type alongside Users, as well as attributes on the User resource "roles" and "entitlements". There are SCIM-enabled applications that support the user.roles attribute and do not support the group resource type. 

We probably need to figure out what the actual protocol-agnostic requirement is and then map it into SCIM requirements.

issues.title: Does AL1 need a requirement to support groups?
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
https://github.com/jischr/scim-ipsie-profiles/blob/c289a468cd17d84b1878d9c33494e8c58e1559cb/draft-schreiber-ipsie-scim-al1-profile.md?plain=1#L239

Probably related to https://github.com/jischr/scim-ipsie-profiles/issues/4

Not all apps have a need to support groups. If they support something like "roles" or "entitlements" then that provides another way for the IDP to view and manage access in the app. Groups have a downside for entitlement granting into apps as well, as the SCIM group resource created by the client in the app can have any name (displayName is an arbitrary label) and what permissions are assigned to the group (and inherited by its members) is generally not visible to the IDP.

comments.author: jischr
comments.body:
so i think this issue is two fold. 

first, first is aroudn SPs not needing groups. could be resolved with:
- The IdP MUST support Group operations
- The SP MAY support Groups if it aligns with their use case

Second point is clarification of what a group is:
Should the profile distinguish between Groups as organizational units the IdP owns and pushes, versus Application-native roles the IdP can read but doesn't manage?

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body:
> Should the profile distinguish between Groups as organizational units the IdP owns and pushes, versus Application-native roles the IdP can read but doesn't manage?

SCIM has both of these concepts with the same names that you used here, and both are regularly in use with current SCIM implementations, so I think we should address both of them separately. I'm in favor of referring to them using the existing SCIM terminology, and if necessary, we can add items to the terminology section near the beginning of the document.

> first, first is aroudn SPs not needing groups. could be resolved with:
> 

- > The IdP MUST support Group operations

- > The SP MAY support Groups if it aligns with their use case

I think the second option is the correct one. Virtually everything in SCIM is optional when it comes to the schema and what resources are supported, and not all applications have need for groups and/or roles. There's an argument that having some way for the IDP to see and/or manage entitlement grants in the application improves security posture. If I were to try to write a SCIM AL* requirement to capture that, it would probably be a requirement for the SP to support at least one of a list of methods that help to achieve that. 

Given the multiple options that are available, IMO we should provide requirements that apply if the application supports one of those features. I'm not sure if we should be mandating either of them at AL1, though - would need to think about that more and discuss with a wider group.

issues.title: Explicitly disallow SCIM SPs from supporting the user "password" attribute
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
https://github.com/jischr/scim-ipsie-profiles/blob/c289a468cd17d84b1878d9c33494e8c58e1559cb/draft-schreiber-ipsie-scim-al1-profile.md?plain=1#L117

Not sure where to put the requirement, but I think we should add one that explicitly disallows SCIM SPs from supporting the user "password" attribute. Federation/SSO should be required, which means that the "password" attribute on the User resource shouldn't be needed. There are legacy apps that may require passwords to be synced into them, but those won't be IPSIE SL* compliant and similarly shouldn't be AL* compliant, IMO. 

I'm not sure if a requirement is needed or useful on the IDP side - the IDP's client/provisioning service will always support a superset of features compared to what any single application may use, and an IDP's SCIM client supporting sending the user "password" attribute doesn't matter if it isn't being used with the SCIM SP. I can think of some possible implementation mistakes that could lead to security issues, such as mapping IDP's user.password to any random attribute on the application's end, and then using that to discover the user's password in the IDP - but my gut is that that isn't in IPSIE's scope.

comments.author: jischr
comments.body:
@Zollnerd - i think this is valid. just a few questions for discussion:

Should the Application reject the entire request if password is included, or only reject the password attribute itself?
For example, if a POST /Users includes password alongside otherwise valid attributes, does the whole create fail, or should the Application create the user and ignore/reject only that attribute?

Does this extend to extension schemas?
An Application could technically accept password-equivalent credential material under a custom schema namespace, and the current language wouldn’t catch that.

Is the intent to prohibit only the core SCIM User.password attribute, or is the intention requirement broader i.e., prohibiting any attribute that carries credential material (hashed passwords, MFA seeds, recovery codes, etc.)?

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body:
> Should the Application reject the entire request if password is included, or only reject the password attribute itself? 
> For example, if a POST /Users includes password alongside otherwise valid attributes, does the whole create fail, or should the Application create the user and ignore/reject only that attribute?

The object's schema is defined by the application, so the most critical requirement is going to be that the application MUST not support the password attribute. 

RFC 7644 gives pretty broad discretion to the SCIM service provider to alter or ignore parts of incoming requests - both what attributes are included, and their values.  In practice, some service providers will silently drop unsupported attributes on a POST, and others will return an error due to the inclusion of unsupported attributes. 

> Does this extend to extension schemas?
> An Application could technically accept password-equivalent credential material under a custom schema namespace, and the current language wouldn’t catch that.

> Is the intent to prohibit only the core SCIM User.password attribute, or is the intention requirement broader i.e., prohibiting any attribute that carries credential material (hashed passwords, MFA seeds, recovery codes, etc.)?

Good catch. RFC 7643 section 3.3 has a normative requirement related to this:
`_Schema extensions SHOULD avoid redefining any attributes defined in this specification and SHOULD follow conventions defined in this specification._`

That SHOULD is a problem, as is the difference in interpretation that various people may have when it comes to whether or not an extension is redefining attributes defined in RFC 7643.  

When I created this issue, I was thinking only of user.password, but I think there's value in determining what is allowed, and for the things that are allowed, what the rules are.  

I'll add language around user.password to the current edits I'm working on, and I'll create a new issue to track the other scenarios.

issues.title: Requirement for IDP to deactivate within X minutes
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
https://github.com/jischr/scim-ipsie-profiles/blob/c289a468cd17d84b1878d9c33494e8c58e1559cb/draft-schreiber-ipsie-scim-al1-profile.md?plain=1#L140

I'm not sure how practical this requirement is at 5 minutes. SCIM APIs usually have request rate limits that lead to SCIM clients building an outgoing message queue to avoid triggering 429 responses from the SCIM API. These queues usually operate on a FIFO (first in, first out) model, although inserting specific requests to the top of the queue is possible. For larger source directories with hundreds of thousands of users, the churn in the directory combined with any "transient" deactivations that may have the user go from active -> disabled -> active in the span of a few minutes could end up with the active true/false changes consuming most or all of the SCIM API's request rate allowance, keeping other changes stuck in that outgoing message queue for a while. 

An example of the transient deactivation I mentioned above is: the user signs in from new location, a risk event triggers that leads them to lose access to some apps/have sign-in at the IDP blocked/etc., and then they mitigate the "high risk" flag via something like strong MFA.

Any requirement on the AL* side should probably take the existence/use of other mechanisms to disable an account (CAEP?, OpenID Provider Commands..) since if another mechanism that can accomplish the same thing is in use requiring it with SCIM AL1 may not have any benefit, but it will increase COGS for both the SCIM client and SCIM service provider, as well as consuming the SCIM client's request allowance with the SCIM service provider.

comments.author: jischr
comments.body:

issues.title: Remove "Application MUST allow the creation of a new user with the same username."
issues.author: jischr
issues.body:
**Existing Text:**
> Delete User (DELETE /Users/{id})
> Applications MAY allow users to be deleted via the SCIM operation DELETE /Users/{id}.

> After a user is deleted, the Application MUST allow the creation of a new user with the same username.

> Editor's Note: Need to clarify implications for maintaining user data and avoiding conflicts when recreating users with the same username.

**Remove:**
- "Application MUST allow the creation of a new user with the same username." 


Ref:
- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7644#section-3.6

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body:
Leaning toward removing this sentence. The SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile, which this profile requires conformance with, already covers it in its Resource Lifecycle section: after a resource is successfully deleted, its unique identifiers such as `userName` MUST NOT be considered in uniqueness checks and MUST be available for reassignment. Restating it here is redundant.

A related point to decide alongside this: the Interop Profile's Identifier Reuse section notes that reusing `userName` and similar values after a delete can attach access to the wrong person, and that a Service Provider that wants to prevent reuse should retain the resource with `active` set to `false` rather than deleting it. Should this profile say the Identity Service SHOULD deprovision by setting `active` to `false`, and use `DELETE` only when explicitly configured to? That depends on #28, which lets an Application support either mechanism.

Leaving both open for now.

issues.title: Move the 5 minute propagation requirement to the IPSIE Account Lifecycle spec
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Line 141 currently reads:

> The Identity Service SHOULD propagate user deactivation events to the Application within 5 minutes of the user being deactivated.

This is a timing requirement on the Identity Service's propagation behavior, not something specific to the SCIM protocol mechanics covered by this profile. It should be defined once, globally, at the IPSIE Account Lifecycle level, and referenced (not restated) here, rather than being defined specifically within the SCIM Account Lifecycle profile.

issues.title: Remove the 5 minute revocation requirement on line 143
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Line 143 currently reads:

> The Application SHOULD respond to user deactivation events by revoking the ability for the user to continue accessing the Application, including the revocation of currently active sessions. Session revocation mechanisms are outside the scope of this profile. Revocation SHOULD occur within 5 minutes of receiving the deactivation request.

SCIM is a synchronous protocol: when the Identity Service (SCIM client) makes a request to deactivate or delete a user, the Application (SCIM service provider) processes that request synchronously in the response cycle. There is no meaningful additional delay for the Application to introduce here, so a separate "within 5 minutes of receiving the deactivation request" timing requirement is unnecessary. The requirement should be removed; a timely synchronous response to the SCIM request is adequate.

issues.title: To-do: define AL actions and map them to specific SCIM protocol requests
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Open to-do: the IPSIE WG should define the set of Account Lifecycle (AL) actions, and this profile should then map each defined AL action to the specific SCIM protocol request(s) that implement it.

Filing here to track within this repo as well as raising with the IPSIE WG, since the SCIM-side mapping work depends on the AL action definitions landing at the IPSIE Account Lifecycle level.

issues.title: Client authentication requirements contradict each other (JWT client auth vs. HTTP Basic)
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The client authentication bullets in the Authentication and Authorization section cannot all be satisfied at once. See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L111-L115

- L111 requires the `client_credentials` grant with JWT client authentication ([RFC 7523 §2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7523#section-2.2)). That mechanism sends `client_assertion` and `client_assertion_type` as form parameters in the token request body ([RFC 7521 §4.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7521#section-4.2)).
- L113 requires HTTP Basic authentication and prohibits `client_assertion` in the request body. A signed JWT assertion cannot be carried in HTTP Basic.
- L115 requires the Identity Service to publish RFC 8414 *authorization server* metadata with a `jwks_uri` so the Application can validate "JWTs it issues." Under §2.2 the Identity Service is an OAuth *client*. The Application's authorization server finds a client's public keys through client metadata (`jwks_uri`, [RFC 7591 §2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591#section-2)) or configuration, not AS metadata.

The intent of L113 was to strengthen RFC 6749 §2.3.1, which makes sending client credentials in the request body NOT RECOMMENDED, so that shared secrets are not sent in the body. Requiring `private_key_jwt` achieves that goal, because no shared secret exists.

## Proposed change

- L111: keep. Clarify that the Identity Service authenticates with `private_key_jwt`, sending `client_assertion` in the token request body per RFC 7521 §4.2 / RFC 7523 §2.2.
- L113: replace with a requirement that client authentication methods using shared secrets (`client_secret_basic`, `client_secret_post`) MUST NOT be used.
- L115: keep the Application's AS metadata and `token_endpoint`. Replace the Identity Service's AS metadata requirement with a requirement that it publish its client public keys at a `jwks_uri`, which the Application's authorization server uses to validate client assertions.

## Related

- #11 (resolved by this)
- #9 (future JWT-bearer + DPoP)
- PR #22

issues.title: AL1: require support for at least one of user deactivation (active) or DELETE
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

AL1 requires the Identity Service to be able to locate a user and remove their access. The draft implies a specific mechanism and is internally inconsistent about it:

- The deactivate/reactivate section assumes `PATCH` on `active`. See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L137-L154
- `DELETE` is MAY. See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L156-L158
- The Compliance Statement says the AL1 Application SHALL support both. See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L293
- `active` and `userName` are only required at AL2. See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L185-L193

## Proposed change

- The Application MUST support at least one of:
  - deactivation by setting `active` to `false` via `PATCH /Users/{id}` (in which case `active` MUST be defined in the User schema), or
  - `DELETE /Users/{id}`.
- The Application MAY support both.
- Make the Compliance Statement match.
- Move attributes needed for AL1 lookup (at least `userName`) into an AL1 schema section.
- The reactivation requirement at L154 applies only if the Application supports `active` (see also #12).
- The AL1 filter list (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L170-L175) references `emails` and `externalId`, which are not required at AL1. The SCIM Interop Profile requires a 400 `invalidFilter` for filters on undefined attributes. Make each filter requirement conditional on the Application supporting the attribute it references.

## Related

- Discovery of which mechanism(s) an Application supports is filed separately (#29).
- #12

issues.title: Discovery of supported deprovisioning mechanism(s): active vs. DELETE
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

If AL1 allows an Application to support either `active`-based deactivation or `DELETE /Users/{id}` (or both, see #28), the Identity Service needs to know which one(s) are available.

- Support for `active` can be inferred from whether the attribute appears in the User schema at `/Schemas`.
- Support for `DELETE` cannot be discovered. SCIM has no `ServiceProviderConfig` or `ResourceTypes` metadata indicating which HTTP methods a resource type supports, so a client can only find out by sending the request.
- When both are supported, nothing tells the Identity Service which one the Application prefers or what each one means locally (e.g., whether `DELETE` is a hard delete or a soft delete).

Relevant text: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L137-L162

## Options

- Rely on schema inference for `active` and attempt/fall back for `DELETE` (no new metadata).
- Define per-resource-type operation support metadata. This likely belongs in the SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile or a SCIM extension rather than this profile, for example new `ServiceProviderConfig` values or an extension to the `ResourceType` schema.
- Configuration out of band (status quo in most deployments).

## Next step

Decide whether IPSIE needs this at all, and if so, raise it with the SCIM WG / Interop Profile rather than defining it here.

issues.title: AL2: make group requirements conditional on the Application supporting Groups
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

AL2's defining expansion over AL1 is full user lifecycle management: create, update, and list users, in addition to locating and deactivating or deleting them. Group support is optional (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L219), but two passages read as if group sync is mandatory:

- The AL2 summary describes AL2 as the Identity Service synchronizing user provisioning *and group membership*. See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L53
- The Application "MUST support mapping Identity Service groups to local Application roles and capabilities." See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L179

## Proposed change

- Rewrite L53 so AL2 is described as full user lifecycle management, with group and membership synchronization described as applying when the Application supports Groups.
- Make L179 conditional: "If the Application supports Groups, it MUST support mapping..."
- The level name ("User and Group Management") comes from IPSIE Levels terminology. This issue does not propose renaming it, but the WG may want to.

## Related

- #5

issues.title: Remove the SCIM /Bulk requirements
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The Performance and Efficiency section requires both parties to support `/Bulk` and recommends the Identity Service use it above 100 resources in 5 minutes. See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L128 and https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L131

- `/Bulk` is one of the least widely implemented SCIM features on both the client and service provider side. Requiring it would likely keep most current implementations from conforming.
- Bulk has its own partial-failure semantics (`failOnErrors`, `bulkId` cross-references), which add a new source of implementation variation rather than reducing one.
- The 100-resources-in-5-minutes threshold has no stated basis.
- The SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile, which this profile requires, makes `/Bulk` OPTIONAL.
- The citation is wrong: `/Bulk` is defined in RFC 7644 §3.7, not RFC 7643 §3.7.

## Proposed change

Delete both bullets. `/Bulk` support remains OPTIONAL per the Interop Profile. This can be revisited if deployment evidence supports requiring it.

issues.title: Replace "required functionality as defined in RFC 7643/7644" with a conform-as-implemented rule
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The draft requires the Identity Service and Application to implement "the required functionality" of a SCIM client and service provider as defined in RFC 7643 and RFC 7644. See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L120-L121

The RFCs do not define a clean required feature set. Read broadly, these bullets would require features this profile deliberately leaves out, such as `POST /Users` at AL1, or Groups when the Application does not support them.

## Proposed change

Replace both bullets with a rule that, for every resource type, endpoint, operation, and attribute an implementation supports (whether or not this profile requires it), the implementation MUST behave as specified by the specification defining that feature: RFC 7643 and RFC 7644 as modified by the SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile and this profile, or, for features from later SCIM extensions, the specification that defines them (e.g., RFC 9865 for cursor pagination).

issues.title: AL1: Identity Service must be able to locate and link existing accounts it did not create
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

At AL1 the Identity Service may not have created the account at the Application. It may have been created by SSO just-in-time (JIT) provisioning, by a local administrator, or by an import, so `externalId` is empty. The Identity Service has to locate the correct account before it can deactivate or delete it. The draft lists supported filters (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L168-L175) but does not say which attribute identifies the person. If the account the Identity Service finds over SCIM is not the account the user signs in to via SSO, deprovisioning silently misses the user.

## Proposed change

- The Application MUST support `eq` filtering on the User attribute it uses to match SSO sign-ins to local accounts (e.g., `userName` or `emails.value`), and MUST document which attribute that is.
- The Identity Service MUST use that attribute to locate the account. The Identity Service MAY also query other attributes the Application enforces uniqueness on (e.g., `emails.value`, `employeeNumber`). An account can hold a conflicting value in one of those attributes even when the SSO matching attribute differs between the two systems (in which case SSO would fail, or JIT would create a duplicate user), and those accounts also need to be found.
- The Identity Service MAY set `externalId` on the account after linking, and the Application MUST accept that update, including at AL1.

## Related

- #28
- #29

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body: Implemented in #50 with a narrower scope than proposed above. Instead of requiring the Application to expose and document the attribute it uses for SSO matching, and defining how the Identity Service looks users up, the change requires the Application to accurately advertise every User attribute it enforces uniqueness on through the `uniqueness` characteristic at `/Schemas` (always including `userName`). How the Identity Service uses those attributes is left to the Identity Service. Setting `externalId` after linking applies only if the Application supports `externalId`.

issues.title: Deactivated users must remain visible via GET and filter queries
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

Some Applications omit inactive users from GET and filter results. The Identity Service then cannot confirm a deactivation, cannot reactivate the user, and may create a duplicate. See: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L137-L154 and https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L164-L175

## Proposed change

When the Application supports `active`, a User with `active: false` MUST continue to be returned by `GET /Users/{id}` and by filter queries, with `active` set to `false`.

## Related

- #28

issues.title: Reactivation must not restore credentials revoked at deactivation
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The draft requires all access mechanisms to be deactivated when a user is deactivated (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L145-L152) and requires that reactivation be possible (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L154). It does not say what happens to those mechanisms on reactivation. If an Application only suspends API tokens, personal access tokens, refresh tokens, or sessions, reactivating the user restores credentials that may have been exposed while the account was inactive.

## Proposed change

API tokens, personal access tokens, refresh tokens, sessions, SSH keys, and other credentials revoked at deactivation MUST NOT be restored when the user is reactivated. The user must establish new ones.

## Open question: where this requirement belongs

This requirement is about the Application's credential and session handling, not about SCIM. Options:

- This profile (SCIM AL), alongside the deactivation requirements it qualifies.
- A protocol-independent core document for all IPSIE AL profiles, so it applies equally to AL profiles for other protocols not yet specified.
- IPSIE Session Lifecycle, since it governs sessions and tokens.
- A general IPSIE document above both SL and AL, since it spans both.

The same question applies to the existing list of access mechanisms to deactivate (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L145-L152).

## Related

- #12

issues.title: AL1: specify the deactivation request and limit required PATCH support to active
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The deactivate/reactivate section (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L137-L139) does not define the request. Through the SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile, an AL1 Application inherits the full PATCH grammar for every attribute, which is more than a deprovisioning-only level needs.

## Proposed change

- Define deactivation as `PATCH /Users/{id}` with `{"op":"replace","path":"active","value":false}`, and reactivation as the same with `true`.
- At AL1, the Application is only required to accept PATCH operations on `active` (and `externalId`, if #33 is adopted). It MAY reject PATCH operations on other attributes. Full PATCH support is required at AL2.

## Related

- #28
- #33

issues.title: Deprovisioning triggers should include loss of access to the Application, not only user deactivation
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The AL1 text frames deprovisioning around the user being deactivated in the Identity Service (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L135 and https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L141). In practice the more common trigger is a user who remains active in the Identity Service but loses access to this Application, because they were unassigned from it or removed from the group that grants access.

## Proposed change

The Identity Service MUST deactivate or delete the user at the Application whenever the user is no longer entitled to access it. That includes the user being deactivated or deleted in the Identity Service, and the user's assignment to the Application being removed.

## Related

- #23
- #24

issues.title: Define IPSIE AL conformance identifiers for conformsTo.profiles
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile defines `conformsTo.profiles` in `ServiceProviderConfig` so a Service Provider can declare which profiles it conforms to. This profile defines no identifiers for its levels, so an Application cannot declare AL1 or AL2 conformance in a machine-readable way, and an Identity Service or OIDF certification cannot check it.

Compliance Statement: https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L287-L302

## Proposed change

- Define a URI for each level.
- An Application conforming at a level MUST list that level's identifier, along with the Interop Profile's identifier. Because levels are cumulative, an AL2 Application lists both AL1 and AL2.

## Open question

Should the identifiers be OIDF-namespaced URLs (the Interop Profile permits unregistered URIs), or URNs registered in the IANA "SCIM Profile Identifiers" registry the Interop Profile proposes?

issues.title: Look up existing users before create; actionable 409 uniqueness errors
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The draft does not say how the Identity Service avoids creating duplicate accounts (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L203-L205), or what it does when a create fails with a uniqueness conflict.

## Proposed change

- Before `POST /Users`, the Identity Service SHOULD query the Application with `eq` filters on the User attributes the Application enforces uniqueness on. The SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile requires filter support for those attributes.
- If a `POST` still returns `409` with `scimType` `uniqueness` (e.g., not every unique attribute was checked, or a lookup returned unexpected results), the Identity Service SHOULD attempt to locate the existing account rather than treating the create as a terminal failure. If the error response identifies the conflicting attribute(s), the Identity Service uses those. Otherwise it queries each uniqueness-constrained attribute present in the request.
- When the Application returns `409` with `scimType` `uniqueness`, the error response MUST identify the attribute(s) whose values caused the conflict.

## Notes

- The SCIM error response ([RFC 7644 §3.12](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7644#section-3.12)) has no structured field for an attribute name, only the human-readable `detail`. Putting attribute names in `detail` helps operators but is not reliably machine-parseable. A structured field (e.g., an error extension) would let the Identity Service act on it automatically. That may belong in the SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile, which already defines the 409/`uniqueness` requirement, rather than here.
- The Application should not include other resources' attribute values in the error (e.g., another user's email) beyond what the request itself contained.

## Related

- #33

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body: Implemented in #50. The 409 recovery text was reduced to "SHOULD attempt to locate and link to the existing user rather than treating the request as a terminal failure", without prescribing which attributes the Identity Service queries. The error response must identify the conflicting attribute(s), for example "Uniqueness conflict with attribute userName", and SHOULD NOT include anything else, such as the conflicting value or information about the existing resource.

issues.title: Should group-to-role mappings be keyed on group id rather than displayName?
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The draft addresses `displayName` uniqueness for groups (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L230-L232) but says nothing about how the Application keys its mapping from groups to local roles and capabilities (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L179). `displayName` can be renamed and, after a group is deleted, reused. A mapping keyed on the name can then grant a role to the wrong group or silently stop applying. The SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile's Identifier Reuse section makes the same argument for Users.

## Options

- (a) The Application MUST key group-to-role mappings on the group's `id`.
- (b) SHOULD rather than MUST.
- (c) Out of scope: mapping is internal to the Application and not externally testable.

## Status

Undecided. Filed for discussion.

## Related

- #30

issues.title: Add Delete Group (DELETE /Groups/{id}) requirements
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The Compliance Statement says the AL2 Identity Service initiates "all CRUD operations" for Groups (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L296). The draft has Create, Get, List, and Update sections for Groups (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L217-L264), but no Delete.

## Proposed change

- Add a Delete Group section: if the Application supports Groups, it MUST support `DELETE /Groups/{id}`.
- Deleting a group MUST remove any access its members held through that group.

## Open question

MUST, or MAY to parallel `DELETE /Users/{id}` (see #28)? Unlike Users, a group has no `active` attribute to fall back on. Removing all of a group's members leaves the group in place, so without `DELETE`, groups the Identity Service creates would remain in the Application indefinitely unless an administrator removes them through some other means.

## Related

- #30

issues.title: Application must honor excludedAttributes=members on /Groups
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The Identity Service SHOULD include `excludedAttributes=members` when listing groups (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L244), but nothing requires the Application to honor it. An Application that ignores the parameter returns full membership lists for every group, which defeats the purpose for large groups and can make listing groups impractical.

## Proposed change

If the Application supports Groups, it MUST support the `excludedAttributes` parameter with a value of `members` on `GET /Groups` and `GET /Groups/{id}`, and MUST omit `members` from the response when it is specified.

## Related

- #30

issues.title: Scope of the "local modifications are prohibited" requirement
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

"Local modifications to Users or Groups in the Application are prohibited" (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L122) is a Shared Prerequisite, so it applies at AL1. At AL1, though, accounts are expected to be created and managed locally: the Identity Service only locates and deprovisions them. The requirement also does not say which attributes or which users it covers (e.g., break-glass administrators, users the Identity Service does not manage, Application-specific attributes the Identity Service never sends), or what "local" means.

The AL2 wording (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L179), "MUST prohibit local account creation for users managed by the Identity Service," is circular: a locally created user is by definition not managed by the Identity Service.

## What counts as "local"

A modification made through a SCIM or API connection from an identity service is different from an administrator manually creating or editing a user in the Application's admin UI. Applications may have more than one identity service connected (e.g., during a migration between IdPs, or when different identity services manage different populations), and a change made by a second identity service over its own connection should not be treated as a local modification. For example, a user deactivated by one identity service might legitimately be reactivated by another.

## Options

- Define "local modification" as a change made through the Application's own UI or administrative tooling, as distinct from changes made by any identity service over a SCIM or API connection.
- AL1: a user that has been deactivated by an identity service MUST NOT be reactivatable through local means. Reactivation by an identity service (the same one or another connected one) remains allowed.
- AL2: for Users and Groups provisioned by an identity service, the attributes that identity service manages MUST NOT be locally modifiable. Other attributes remain locally editable.
- Explicitly permit or prohibit SSO just-in-time provisioning alongside SCIM. It is common in practice.
- Carve out break-glass or local administrator accounts.

## Status

Undecided. Filed for discussion.

## Related

- #33
- #12

issues.title: Future AL level: Identity Service reconciliation
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The profile's introduction lists "synchronization of data from the Identity Service to the Application" as a focus (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L63), but no requirement ensures the Application's state actually converges with the Identity Service's. Missed or failed requests, out-of-band changes at the Application, and outages all cause drift that event-driven provisioning alone does not correct. Without a reconciliation requirement, "Get All Users" (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L211-L215) has no defined purpose in the profile.

## Proposal

Treat reconciliation as a capability of a future AL level (AL3 or later) rather than adding it to AL2. A requirement at that level might say:

- The Identity Service MUST periodically reconcile its view of each User (and each Group, if supported) with the Application using `GET /Users` and `GET /Groups`, and MUST correct any divergence in attributes it manages.
- A minimum reconciliation frequency, and whether the Application must support the pagination and request volume needed for a full read at that frequency.

## Open questions

- Which level? AL3 is currently scoped to Role Management (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L266-L270). Reconciliation could join AL3 or form its own level.
- Should AL2 include a SHOULD as a stepping stone?
- What does "correct divergence" mean for attributes the Identity Service does not manage? See #43.

## Status

Undecided. Filed for discussion.

issues.title: Define the audit logging requirement
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The Security Considerations section says all SCIM requests that create, delete, or modify a resource "SHALL be logged for audit and troubleshooting" (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L280). As written, it cannot be implemented consistently or tested:

- **Who logs.** It does not say whether the Application, the Identity Service, or both log. Each sees different failures: the Identity Service knows which requests it decided to send and why; the Application knows which requests it received and rejected.
- **What is logged.** No fields are specified. A useful minimum: timestamp; the authenticated client (OAuth `client_id` or connection identifier); HTTP method and resource path; target resource `id`; outcome (HTTP status and `scimType`, if any); and which attributes were changed.
- **What is not logged.** Nothing prohibits logging sensitive material. Credentials, secrets, client assertions, access tokens, and similar values must never be logged by either party, and logs should identify changed attributes without recording sensitive attribute values.
- **Which requests.** Only successful writes are covered. Rejected or failed write attempts matter as much for security monitoring and troubleshooting.
- **Who can access the logs.** For enterprise customers, the useful property is that the tenant's administrator can see SCIM activity for their tenant (through the admin UI, an export, or an API). Logs visible only to the vendor do not support customer audits or incident response.
- **Retention.** No minimum retention period is stated. Compliance frameworks commonly expect a defined retention period; the value needs research before it is specified.
- **Correlation.** There is no way to correlate an Identity Service log entry with the corresponding Application log entry (e.g., a request identifier present in both).
- **Placement.** The requirement uses normative language under Security Considerations. It may belong in Shared Prerequisites, or in a protocol-independent IPSIE document (see #35 for the same question about credential revocation).

## Proposed direction (to be decided)

- The Application MUST log every SCIM request that creates, modifies, or deletes a resource, whether it succeeded or was rejected, recording at least the fields listed above.
- The Application MUST make those logs available to the tenant administrator.
- The Identity Service MUST log every SCIM request it sends and the response outcome.
- The Application and the Identity Service MUST NOT log credentials, secrets, client assertions, access tokens, or similar values. This applies to all logging under this profile.

## Open questions

- Should authentication and authorization failures at the Application's SCIM endpoints (and at its OAuth token endpoint) also be required to be logged?
- Should read requests be logged, given their volume?
- What minimum retention period, if any?
- Should a request correlation mechanism be defined?

## Related

- #6 (closed; clarified the scope of logged "provisioning actions")
- #35

issues.title: Rework the replay resistance requirement
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The Security Considerations section requires that "access tokens SHALL expire and nonces SHALL be validated to prevent replay" (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L279). The `client_credentials` grant has no nonce, so the second half cannot be applied as written, and the first half sets no bound on token lifetime.

## Options

- The Application's authorization server MUST reject a client assertion whose `jti` has already been used within the assertion's validity period ([RFC 7523 §3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7523#section-3)).
- Client assertions MUST have a short `exp`.
- Access tokens MUST have a bounded lifetime, with a stated maximum.
- Reference sender-constrained access tokens (DPoP, [RFC 9449](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9449)) as the future direction.

## Note: a separate IPSIE document for workload authentication?

These requirements, and the client authentication requirements in #27, are not specific to SCIM. They apply to any workload or non-human identity (NHI) calling an API on another party's behalf. IPSIE may want a separate document for workload/NHI authentication and authorization that this profile (and other IPSIE profiles) reference, rather than each profile defining its own.

## Related

- #27
- #9

issues.title: Group displayName uniqueness: require uniqueness, or another unique group identifier
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The Group Schema section says Applications SHOULD NOT allow multiple groups
with the same displayName:
https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L230-L232

RFC 7643 Section 8.7.1 gives displayName a uniqueness of "none" and Section
4.2 does not require it to be unique, so a SHOULD NOT leaves Applications free
to allow duplicates. That has two consequences:

1. A retried POST /Groups after a timeout or 5xx can create a second group,
   because there is no uniqueness conflict to return. For Users, userName
   gives the Identity Service a 409 that signals the earlier request
   succeeded. Groups have nothing equivalent.
2. The List Groups By Alternate Identifier requirement
   (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L252-L256)
   requires displayName eq, but if displayName is not unique the filter can
   return several groups and the Identity Service cannot tell which one it
   created or manages.

Proposal: for Applications that implement Groups, replace the SHOULD NOT with
a requirement that the Application either enforce uniqueness of displayName
or provide another attribute that is unique, mutable, and human-readable, and
that the Identity Service can use to identify a group (similar to userName and
emails for Users). In both cases:

- the attribute's uniqueness is advertised in /Schemas,
- the Application supports eq filtering on it, and
- a uniqueness conflict returns 409 with scimType uniqueness.

displayName has caseExact false in RFC 7643, so uniqueness of displayName
should be case-insensitive, matching the treatment of userName.

The alternative attribute lets Applications that cannot make displayName
unique without a breaking change comply without changing displayName.

This came out of review of the SCIM Interoperability Profile
(draft-zollner-scim-interop-profile), where resource-specific Group attribute
requirements were left to this profile.

issues.title: Remove the "SHOULD avoid returning more than 1,000 users per page" recommendation
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

The draft says the Application SHOULD avoid returning more than 1,000 users per page, and recommends cursor-based pagination (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L215). The SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile already governs page size (a default of at least 100, support for client `count` of at least 100, truncation to the server maximum) and requires Clients to support both index-based and cursor-based pagination. A second number with no stated basis adds a parallel rule without improving interoperability.

## Proposed change

Remove the sentence, including the cursor recommendation. Page size and pagination method are governed by the Interop Profile.

issues.title: Consolidate rate limiting requirements; keep minimum throughput and define tenant
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
## Problem

Rate limiting appears twice in this draft (https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L126-L127 and https://github.com/openid/ipsie-scim-al/blob/1a9985f987526395d7aeaa2600108b236e49a7cf/draft-openid-ipsie-al-scim-profile.md?plain=1#L281) and again in the SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile:

- "MUST enforce rate limits on all SCIM endpoints" is not testable: an Application enforcing a very high limit is indistinguishable from one enforcing none.
- L126 refers to "headers, such as 429 Too Many Requests". 429 is an HTTP status code ([RFC 6585 §4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6585#section-4)), not a header.
- The Interop Profile already specifies the response when a limit is exceeded (429 or 503 with `Retry-After`, and client backoff).

## Proposed change

- Replace L126 and L281 with a reference to the Interop Profile's rate limiting requirements.
- Keep the minimum throughput at L127 (25 requests per second per tenant) as the IPSIE-specific requirement, and define "tenant", including whether the minimum applies per tenant or per Identity Service connection when a tenant has more than one connection.
- Whether a minimum throughput applies to every request type (so an Application cannot meet it on reads alone while throttling writes far below it) is a general SCIM interoperability question. It is being raised against the SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile instead of here: Zollnerd/scim-interop-profile#17

pulls.author: Zollnerd
pulls.body: Sweeping set of edits to the IPSIE AL1 draft to add new requirements, remove some non-normative text, and reorganize some of the content.

comments.body: do we want to reject the password attribute? ie return a 400?
this may want to become a stricter requirement in the future.
As it is that requirement says they MUST support a pagination method. What are you thinking for making it stricter?
That depends on the implementation and the HTTP method being used. The SCIM spec gives more leeway to silently ignoring things it doesn't like in a POST, but a PATCH would have to return a 400, IIRC.

pulls.title: scim interop feedback al1 migration
pulls.author: Zollnerd
pulls.body:
- Adds a normative conformance requirement: AL1 implementations MUST also
  conform to `draft-zollner-scim-interop-profile`, inheriting its requirements
  for endpoint structure, resource lifecycle, discovery endpoints, PATCH/PUT
  behavior, TLS, and filtering.

- Removes requirements from AL1 now fully covered by that reference:
  PATCH/PUT restriction, pagination MUST, general filter support statements,
  metadata endpoint requirements, TLS minimum version,
  `attributes=`/`excludedAttributes=` MUST.

- Retains IPSIE-specific requirements: OAuth 2.0 with JWT client auth,
  User/Group attribute requirements, credential prohibition, deactivation
  behavior and timelines, cursor pagination RECOMMENDED, 1,000-result SHOULD
  limit, `excludedAttributes=members` SHOULD guidance for group listing.

- Adds `members[value eq {memberId}]` to required Group filter expressions.

## Summary

- Replace "claims" terminology in AL2 introduction with SCIM-accurate language ("groups and their memberships")
- Clarify client credentials transmission requirement: explicit that credentials go in the Authorization header, not the request body
- Restructure OAuth AS metadata requirements to cover both Application and Identity Service; promote `jwks_uri` to MUST for the Identity Service

pulls.author: Zollnerd
pulls.body:
Changes from a full review of the draft against the SCIM 2.0 Interoperability Profile. Each commit addresses one issue, and the issue explains the reasoning behind the change.

| Commit | Issue |
|---|---|
| Resolve contradictory client authentication requirements | #27 (also closes #11) |
| Remove the "scim" scope requirement | #3 |
| Replace "required functionality" rule with conform-as-implemented | #32 |
| Remove the SCIM /Bulk requirements | #31 |
| Remove the 1,000-users-per-page recommendation | #48 |
| Consolidate rate limiting requirements and define tenant | #49 |
| AL1: require at least one of active deactivation or DELETE | #28 |
| AL1: specify the deactivation request and limit required PATCH | #36 |
| Require deactivated users to remain visible via GET and filters | #34 |
| Include loss of application access as a deprovisioning trigger | #37 |
| AL1: require the ability to locate and link existing users | #33 |
| Look up users before create and make 409 conflicts actionable | #39 |
| AL2: make group requirements conditional on Groups support | #30 |

Not included, still open for discussion: #16, #29, #35, #38, #40 to #46.

Related: whether a minimum request rate must apply to write requests as well as reads is raised against the Interop Profile in Zollnerd/scim-interop-profile#17.

pulls.body:
Editorial cleanups, one commit per item. No normative changes.

- Use "Identity Service" instead of "Identity Provider" in the access token requirement
- Fix the reference to the Role terms, which are defined above the note, not below
- Fix the `/Groups/{id}` path in the Get Group and Update Group headings
- Use `userName` (correct case) in the filter list
- Remove a stray quotation mark in the group `displayName` requirement
- Remove the leftover IETF `area` and `stream` front matter. The front matter will be corrected separately; until then mmark warns about an empty `stream` but still builds.

This branch is based on #50 and should be merged after it. Until #50 merges, this PR's diff also shows #50's commits.
